corrections.claim: BLOCKING, 06_unfolding.mp4: 'over 25 sampled fold frames the end-to-end luminance ramp inside a panel is a median of 2.1 grey levels (max 11) while the step at the crease is a median of 13 and up to 51 grey levels across 2-6 px', and at frame 56 'the upper panel reads 180-188 over its whole 130 px height and then jumps 177 -> 236'.
corrections.what_i_measured: Same clip, same window (x 250-800, y 1150-1780), 46 frames across both fold runs, 59 panels inside 33 detected creases. Net end-to-end ramp inside a panel: median 11.31, max 36.76 grey levels. Max-minus-min inside a panel: median 11.50. Crease step (three px each side of the steepest row): median 24.16, max 62.71, min 9.20. Their reported median (2.1) is a fifth of mine and their reported maximum (11) is my median. At frame 56 the upper panel reads 173-184 smoothed, not 180-188, and the crease runs 170 -> 227, not 177 -> 236. The crease-to-panel ratio that carries the argument is 2.1 in my measurement, not the 6.2 implied by theirs. The rest of the finding holds: mean of the 30 rows nearest a crease minus mean of the 30 farthest has a median of -0.37 grey levels, so there really is no crease highlight and no occlusion valley, and by eye the grey panel and the white panel meet at a hard horizontal seam in every fold frame.

gaps: The currency ledger does not cover the two oldest records. Every entry in MANIFEST.json's checks map says from_this_run: true, and none is false - but the map covers only evidence/logs/, and not even all of it: webpush.txt has no entry, and two reports rest a claim on it. None of the six top-level records (DIFF.json, MANIFEST.json, WHY_MISSING.json, coldstart.json, frames.json, reliability.json) is in the ledger, and the two of those that carry dates carry 2026-09-05T00:28 - coldstart.json and reliability.json's tailscale block - each with later_check status pending because the nodes would not answer when it was re-run at 17:42 on the 9th. So the ledger's clean sweep is true and also does not reach the only stale evidence in the set. Coherence filed that staleness as a minor finding and code.json says plainly that the binding is 'proven by unit test and by a dated earlier record, not by a run today'; both handled it correctly, which is why it is a gap in the apparatus rather than a correction.

No rubric row asks whether the evidence's own checks are sound, and three of them are not: grain.json certifies ok:true against a ratio ceiling its own numbers fail (caught, twice), flat.json's numbers cannot be reproduced from its stated method (not caught), and logs/manifest.json reports dangling entries and ok:true for files that exist (not caught). The one rubric row that reads checks at all reads them as sources, not as instruments.

No rubric row is a transport row, and the mission's first sentence names Tailscale. Everything shot this cycle ran transport: local against 127.0.0.1 under one headless WebKit, on four ports (8480 for thirteen scenes, 8797/8798 for the unpaired ones, 8796 under Chromium for reception). The only record of the app crossing a real tailnet between two nodes is four days old and could not be re-run. Coherence reached it from the one-log side and code.json from the binding side; between them the goal's own transport is evidenced by a dated file and a unit test.

The cycle-over-cycle apparatus does not do what its labels say. Because .previous rotates during the run, DIFF.json's unchanged_at 0.999 and its twelve 'byte for byte the same file' rows compare this capture with itself, and its three 'changed' rows compare two takes of one build. Nothing in evidence/ records what the previous cycle's artifacts looked like, so no judgement of improvement or regression anywhere in this review is supported by the evidence it cites. The manifest's write times are what give it away: nine stills at 17:53-17:57 and 13_messenger_states.png alone at 19:56:19Z, after its scene script was rewritten at 19:28 to add the only 'sync' step in the seventeen.

Three of the review's own numbers disagree with each other and nothing reconciles them: the search chip row is counted at eleven, fourteen and fifteen (it is fifteen); frame 305 of clip 08 is read at 125.09 and at 123.7; and material-truth's own hand.json disagrees with its own handwriting figures (the log measures 500 marks with a best-fit IoU median of 0.693 and p90 0.86, the report measures 172 with a median of 0.797 and p90 0.910). Both handwriting readings support the same conclusion and the log's numbers are quoted correctly by anti-goal, so no correction follows - but a reader given both has no way to tell which sample the row was scored on.

What the evidence does not show at all: a reply that has landed beside the note it answers; a video advancing one frame; either of Moments' other two lenses, behind which its own report puts 154 and 1,340 events; anything on the glass during the 8.9-10.0 second first launch; two screens at once; any Android surface; a lock screen or an installed iOS banner; a gesture producing a feeling, every intensity in the set being a number the harness typed; any device vibrating, the whole haptic layer being 36 specified strings with channel_here: 'page'; and the app emitting a sound. Nine of those are filed by somebody. Three of them - the landed reply, the two unphotographed lenses, and the first-launch screen - need no code at all, only a step added to a scene, and one of them is currently capping a category at its floor.

One artifact was re-shot from the same build after the run with one line changed, and the review read the result as progress. That is the whole of this cycle's evidence-made-rather-than-measured problem, and it is worth saying that it is confined to that: the manifest's from_this_run flags are honest, the two absent artifacts have a measured reason rather than an excuse, the sound mix-in is disclosed in its own log, reception.json disowns its own browser, and the fold clip's blocking finding is a real fault of the build even though its numbers are five times too strong.
verdict: The review is thorough and, on measurement, mostly sound: every present artifact was read by at least four of the six reports, one file in all of evidence/ went unopened, and the numbers I could re-take came back right far more often than not - emotional-transmission's page-translation work is exact to the frame and to the digit, anti-goal's saturation census matches to four places including the mean RGB of the one red band, messenger-reliability's scroll_webkit distribution and 401 findings match entry for entry, and code.json is the one report I could not fault anywhere, its suite reproducing at 160 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed when I ran it myself. Three things need correcting and one of them matters. The material row's blocking finding is real in kind and five times too strong in degree: fold panels do meet at a hard seam with no crease highlight, but the intra-panel ramp is a median of 11.3 grey levels over 59 panels, not 2.1, and the crease step 24.2, not 13 - the ratio that makes it decisive is 2.1, not 6.2. The messenger row's blocking finding is a framing fault filed as a build fault, which is the exact error the briefing warned about: no reply has landed anywhere in the evidence because no scene ever sends one, reliability.json from this same run records reply resolving to its target, and the row that draws a landed reply is already in the source at note.dart:106 and thread.dart:365-374 - so a category is capped at its floor over a picture nobody took. And coherence's seventeen-row judgements block reads a mid-run self-comparison as a cycle of progress: .previous was rotated at 19:16:36 inside a run that started at 17:43:03, twelve of its rows compare a file with itself, and the one artifact it calls most improved is the same build re-shot at 19:56 after its script gained a sync step at 19:28. Coherence's other headline - cursor equals events in all seventeen reports - is false in five of them, though harmlessly so. Against that, the evidence's own instruments are the part of this system with no reader: flat.json's numbers cannot be reproduced from the method it prints, logs/manifest.json contradicts itself and passes, webpush.txt sits outside the currency ledger while two reports quote it, coldstart.json is four days old and was twice waved off on the strength of its filename, and two clips carry an audio track the build never played. Nobody is scored on any of that, which is why it lands here. The three cheapest things this review has established are that a reply, the two unphotographed Moments lenses and the first-launch screen can all be evidenced by editing a scene rather than the app - and that the next capture should rotate .previous before the run and not during it, so that the word 'improved' means something the evidence can carry.
